statutes.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India

sections.sectionTitle: Mandatory written tenancy agreement and registration with Rent Authority
sections.content: No person shall, after the commencement of this Act, let or take on rent any premises except by an agreement in writing, which shall be informed to the Rent Authority by the landlord and tenant jointly, in the form specified, within a period of two months from the date of tenancy agreement.
sections.remedy: Mandates formal written agreement preventing arbitrary verbal tenancy disputes.

sections.sectionTitle: Security Deposit limits and refund timeline
sections.content: The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent, in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent, in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises after making lawful deduction of liability with proper accounting.
sections.remedy: Landlord cannot demand more than 2 months rent as security deposit and must refund it on handover.

sections.sectionTitle: Prohibition of cutting off or withholding essential services
sections.content: No landlord or property manager shall, either by himself or through any person, cut off or withhold any essential supply or service in the premises occupied by the tenant. Essential services include supply of water, electricity, passages, staircase light, conservancy and sanitary services. On application by tenant, Rent Authority may pass immediate interim order restoring supply and impose penalty on landlord.
sections.remedy: Immediate restoration of electricity/water and financial penalty against landlord for illegal disconnection.

sections.sectionTitle: Protection against arbitrary eviction and procedure for repossession
sections.content: No landlord shall evict any tenant during the subsistence of tenancy agreement except by filing an application before the Rent Court on specified grounds: (a) tenant refuses to pay agreed rent for two consecutive months; (b) tenant has parted with possession without consent; (c) misuse of premises causing public nuisance; (d) structural alteration without consent. A landlord cannot forcibly lock out a tenant without a decree from the Rent Court.
sections.remedy: Landlord cannot forcibly evict or throw out belongings without a court decree.

statutes.authority: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India

sections.sectionTitle: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract and statutory notice to quit
sections.content: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable by six months' notice; and a lease of immovable property for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by fifteen days' notice in writing.
sections.remedy: Statutory 15-day written notice required before tenancy termination.

sections.sectionTitle: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee
sections.content: In the absence of a contract to the contrary: (a) lessor is bound to disclose material defects in property; (b) lessor is bound to put lessee in possession; (c) if lessor fails to make repairs after reasonable notice, lessee may make the same himself and deduct expenses from rent with interest.
sections.remedy: Tenant can carry out urgent essential repairs and deduct reasonable expenses from upcoming monthly rent.

grievanceSystems.name: Rent Authority / Rent Court
grievanceSystems.description: Statutory quasi-judicial authority established for expeditious adjudication of tenancy disputes, unreturned security deposits, and illegal eviction without long civil court delays.
grievanceSystems.remedy: File a direct petition before the Rent Authority for recovery of security deposit with 18% per annum interest.
